name: Orders in batches
brief:
A broker takes orders in batches of at most `size`. `items` may be any iterable, even a live feed that is never all in memory, so take the items one at a time and hand each batch on as soon as it is full. The last batch may be shorter. Each batch is a new list.

Write the generator `batches(items, size)`. When `size` is below 1, raise `ValueError` as soon as the first batch is asked for.

Example. `list(batches([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], 3))` is `[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7]]`.
constraints: $1 \le$ `size` for a valid call; `items` can be a list, a string, a `range` or a generator.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Fill a list with a `for` loop over `items` and `yield` it when it reaches `size`, then start a new list. After the loop, yield what is left if anything is.

examples.note: Two full batches and one short one.
No items, no batches: not one empty batch.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value. In a test, `_raised(f)` calls `f` and gives the name of the error it raises, or `'no error'`. `feed()` yields three items and then fails, as a feed that closes would.
notes: A generator hands on each full batch at once, so a feed is read only as far as the batches asked for.
Calling `list(items)` first reads the whole feed, and clearing one shared list empties batches already handed on.
Each item is touched once, so $O(n)$ time and $O(\text{size})$ memory.

planted.slip: `list(items)` reads the whole feed before the first batch, so a live feed is never handed on.
The short batch at the end is never yielded.
Clearing one list and refilling it changes the batches already handed on.
